request.system:
You extract project issues from documents about building grid-scale battery storage sites.
Return JSON that matches the schema exactly.

Definitions and rules:
- An issue is a risk, problem, delay, unanswered dependency, constraint or past incident that affects or could affect programme, cost or handover. Work that is simply complete is not an issue.
- Return one mention per distinct issue in this document. Do not merge unrelated issues. Do not split one issue into several.
- title: at most 10 words, neutral wording, no project name.
- description: one or two plain sentences.
- counterparty_role: who the issue depends on or was caused by. Use one of: DNO, civils contractor, contractor, transformer supplier, LPA, landowner, internal. Use null if none is clear.
- status: open = unresolved as of this document; resolved = the document says it is done or closed; materialised = it has now caused a programme slip or a confirmed adverse date; occurred = a past incident described for the record or as a lesson.
- awaiting_third_party: true if the team is waiting on a response or deliverable from someone outside the project team.
- chase_count: the number of chases or requests the document states for this issue, otherwise null.
- programme_impact: realised if a slip has happened, potential if the document says it could affect the programme, otherwise none_stated.
- triggers: only when the document states a condition or deadline after which the issue becomes critical or the programme is at risk. condition_text must be copied from the document. Resolve deadline_date to yyyy-mm-dd using the document date 2025-02-05: a month name means the last day of that month; "within N weeks" means the document date plus N weeks; "autumn" means 1 September of that year. If it cannot be resolved, use null.
- evidence_quote: copy an exact, contiguous piece of the document text, at most 200 characters, that supports the mention. Do not paraphrase.
- programme: fill only values the document states. Dates as yyyy-mm-dd. Use null otherwise.

# Netherwood - Lessons learned workshop

**Date:** 5 February 2025
**Attendees:** Project delivery, Development, Operations,
Procurement

## What went well
- Construction quality, no significant defects
- Site team / contractor relationship
- HSE record: zero reportable incidents

## What did not

**1. Early warnings were recorded but not escalated.**
Both the planning condition delay and the transformer lead time
appear in weekly reports weeks or months before they affected the
programme. Nobody connected the repetition. The weekly report
format records issues but has no concept of "this is the fifth
week running".

**2. Contractor performance information is not shared between
projects.**
The civils contractor's delay at Netherwood was not known to the
Drumgarve team when they were appointed there.

**3. Handover was incomplete.**
See separate handover status note. Operations inherited open items
with no clear owner.

## Agreed actions
1. Introduce a formal escalation trigger for repeated issues -
   owner: project delivery. **Status at time of writing: not done.**
2. Share contractor performance notes across projects - owner:
   procurement. **Status: not done.**
3. Handover checklist with sign-off - owner: operations.
   **Status: drafted.**
